exposure: Causes of stillbirth classified by the Relevant Condition at Death (ReCoDe) system
cohort: 250 women diagnosed with stillbirth clinically or via ultrasonography after 28 weeks of gestation
finding: The most common cause of stillbirth was hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, followed by other maternal disorders (e.g., anemia, jaundice, heart disease), amniotic fluid issues (e.g., oligohydramnios, meconium-stained liquor), fetal causes (e.g., congenital lethal anomalies, fetal growth restriction), and placental causes (e.g., placental abruption).
mod_finding: 74.8% of stillbirths were delivered vaginally (1.2% instrumental) and the remaining underwent cesarean sections.
